method: Look-through composites from each company's own SEC filings (XBRL companyfacts, parsed by fundamentals.py). A fund with weight w in a company of market value mcap owns w/mcap of it; every measure is the sum of those owned slices of a numerator over the same of a denominator. P/E = sum(w) / sum(w x earnings / mcap), the weighted harmonic mean, losses included ('aggregate loss' when the sum is not positive). EV measures and margins over operating companies only (banks and insurers: P/E, P/B, dividend yield). Growth holds today's ownership fixed: sum(w x X now / mcap) / sum(w x X a year earlier / mcap) - 1. Trailing twelve months, GAAP, as filed; statements converted to US dollars at the run's FX; market value = last close x latest filed share count (per ADR for an ADR); companies aggregated by CIK. Covered = a US listing in SEC's ticker map whose company has usable SEC figures ending no more than 200 days ago, a last close and an FX rate. A composite is shown only when covered companies make up at least 70 pct of the row's weight. No analyst estimates or revisions: there is no free source. A fund's own published figures use other definitions (vendor earnings, losses often excluded) and are a cross-check, not this number.
